title: SAFARI: A Community-Engaged Approach and Dataset of Stereotype Resources in the Sub-Saharan African Context
measurement_description: The paper collected and evaluated stereotypes related to religious identity as one of several demographic and identity axes (including ethnicity, gender, profession, etc.) within four Sub-Saharan African countries (Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa).
findings: Religion was identified as a salient axis for stereotypes, particularly in Nigeria, where it accounted for 8% of the identity axes in the collected stereotypes for that country. The paper's primary finding is the creation of a new dataset (SAFARI) that includes such localized stereotypes, which are currently underrepresented in global resources, and demonstrating that leading AI models endorse these stereotypes.
references: Josh Achiam, Steven Adler, Sandhini Agarwal, Lama Ahmad, Ilge Akkaya, Florencia Leoni Aleman, Diogo Almeida, Janko Altenschmidt, Sam Altman, Shyamal Anadkat, and 1 others. 2023. Gpt-4 technical report. arXiv preprint arXiv:2303.08774.
